//! JSON export. 64-bit integers (seq, raw values) are strings; no NaN.

use super::{ExportDoc, raw_hex};
use crate::time::iso8601_utc_ms;
use serde_json::{Value, json};

fn finite(v: Option<f64>) -> Value {
    v.filter(|x| x.is_finite()).map(Value::from).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
}

pub fn document(doc: &ExportDoc) -> Value {
    let measurements: Vec<Value> = doc
        .measurements
        .iter()
        .map(|s| {
            json!({
                "ts_utc": iso8601_utc_ms(s.ts_ms),
                "ts_ms": s.ts_ms,
                "device_id": s.device_id,
                "tag_id": s.tag_id,
                "value": finite(s.value),
                "raw_value": s.raw_value,
                "text": s.text,
                "unit": s.unit,
                "quality": s.quality.as_str(),
                "exception_code": s.quality.exception_code(),
                "age_ms": s.age_ms.map(|a| a.to_string()),
                "value_ts_utc": s.value_ts_ms.map(iso8601_utc_ms),
                "raw_hex": raw_hex(&s.raw),
                "seq": s.seq.to_string(),
                "profile_id": s.profile_id,
                "profile_version": s.profile_version,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    let commands: Vec<Value> = doc
        .commands
        .iter()
        .map(|c| {
            json!({
                "ts_utc": iso8601_utc_ms(c.ts_ms),
                "session_id": c.session_id,
                "user": c.user,
                "role": c.role,
                "event": c.event,
                "device_id": c.device_id,
                "profile_id": c.profile_id,
                "profile_version": c.profile_version,
                "unit_id": c.unit_id,
                "function": c.function,
                "address": c.address,
                "register_id": c.register_id,
                "command_id": c.command_id,
                "old_value": finite(c.old_value),
                "requested_value": finite(c.requested_value),
                "raw_value_hex": c.raw_value_hex,
                "request_hex": c.request_hex,
                "response_hex": c.response_hex,
                "exception": c.exception,
                "ack": c.ack,
                "readback": c.readback,
                "readback_value": finite(c.readback_value),
                "note": c.note,
            })
        })
        .collect();
    json!({
        "format": "buslink-export",
        "format_version": 1,
        "generated_utc": iso8601_utc_ms(doc.generated_ms),

| `commands` | no | list | Control actions. **Only on `simulated_only` profiles in v1.** |

Now the end-to-end tests (sim task 6): faults as client qualities (S5), fairness with a dead device (S6), control with read-back (S7), write round trip (S10), and historian plus export across a gap.
Two gaps from task 1: `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` was never written, and the disclosure row for the BGT-SMPS facts still points at a "future" profile. Fixing both:

Integration-test files are not covered by clippy's in-test exemptions. I'll widen the file-level allow (test code only) and remove two `drop` calls that do nothing:

Formatting and clippy are clean. As a safety check, I'll run every source file through the write-path guard as if it were newly written, so all of its lines count as added:

The deep run passed: 2 000 cases each for the planner, command priority and starvation properties, in 20 s (release build). Final state of the working tree:
All tasks in both specs are done and ticked: core-protocol 15/15, simulator 6/6. `cargo test --workspace` passes 159 tests (up from 94 at the checkpoint), and clippy, fmt and the hook self-tests are clean. Nothing is committed.

## What was added since the checkpoint

- **Command service tests (core task 12):** `tests/command_wire.rs` and `tests/command_props.rs`. These cover arming expiry and every disarm reason, role checks, out-of-bounds values rejected (never clamped), unit 0 never written, and simulated profiles only writable on simulator links. They also cover:
  - a timed-out write reported as "effect unknown", read back and not retried;
  - no write when the audit log can't be written;
  - "acknowledged" and "read-back mismatch" kept as separate results.
- **Historian (task 13):** `src/historian/`. SQLite in WAL mode. Non-GOOD samples are stored with an empty value, so trends break at gaps. The audit table is append-only, enforced by database triggers. Raw values are kept exactly, including 64-bit integers. Per-minute rollups use GOOD samples only.
- **Export (task 14):** `src/export/` writes CSV, XLSX (Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands) and JSON. Text cells starting with `= + - @`, tab or CR get a leading `'`.
- **Simulator crate (`crates/buslink-sim`, all 6 tasks):** soil sensor, VFD, temperature controller and energy meter models, plus fault injection, an in-memory RTU/MBAP transport and a loopback-only TCP server capped at 8 connections. End-to-end tests run the simulator against the real scheduler, command service, historian and export.
- **Housekeeping:**
  - `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` was missing from task 1; it now lists all 57 runtime dependencies with their licenses.
  - New `rustfmt.toml` with `max_width = 120`, to match how the code was written.
  - `zip` 9.5.1 is a test-only dependency (already pulled in by the XLSX library), used to open exported workbooks.
  - Updated: the disclosure rows for the soil-sensor facts, `docs/profiles/schema-v1.md`, and both design docs.

## Checks run

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace` | 159 passed, 0 failed (core 124, sim 35) |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean |
| Hook self-tests | 88 passed |
| Profile checks (5 bundled profiles) | all valid; one expected warning: `generic-holding` has no source |
| Write-path guard on every crate source file | nothing blocked |
| Deep scheduler run (the one that was interrupted) | 2 000 cases each for planning, command priority and starvation: passed |
| Deep command state-machine run | 5 000 cases: passed |

## Property tests: default case counts and seeds

Every property gets a fixed seed: `0xB0511AC2026 ^ fnv1a(property name) ^ (case × 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)`. To replay one case, set `BUSLINK_PBT_SEED=<seed> BUSLINK_PBT_CASES=1`. Base seeds for the required properties:

| Required property | Test name | Cases | Base seed |
|---|---|---|---|
| CRC against known vectors | `crc_residue` (plus a fixed-vector test) | 2 000 | `0xa2a75003de36e825` |
| Frame encode→decode, read FCs | `read_round_trip_01`–`_04` | 4 × 2 000 | derived from each name |
| Frame encode→decode, write FCs | `write_round_trip` / `sim_write_round_trip` | 1 000 / 500 | `0x41494cd1f51c0795` / `0x60ed645d491eb749` |
| Decoder never panics on random bytes | `no_panic` / `write_decode_no_panic` / `codec_no_panic` | 20 000 / 10 000 / 5 000 | `0xfef94fbef83e8a54` / `0x737956f273db0801` / `0xfffd7dabd095fcc3` |
| Codec round trip, type × word order | `codec_<type>_<order>` | 30 × 1 000 | derived from each name |
| Healthy device never starved by a dead one | `no_starvation` / `sim_fairness` | 300 / 20 | `0x325bde208dc4ccd2` / `0x4a396a31f94cf0be` |
| Never sends without Confirmed, never twice | `command_state_machine` / `command_priority_once` | 500 (about 1 100 frames sent) / 200 | `0x86be683b3f0b1688` / `0x83963778415a0807` |

Other properties: fragmentation 500, block planning 1 000, validator agreement with Python on mutated profiles 400, profile mutation 2 000, formula guard 5 000, rollup vs naive 60, simulator determinism 100, step splitting 100, RTU chunking 200, temperature convergence 30, energy monotonic 20, soil drift 8. Automatic shrinking of failing cases is not available, the trade-off accepted in the design.

## Not done or not verified

- **No hardware tested.** The soil-sensor profile stays `documented`. Its register map comes from the reference project's README and user manual, which cite manual pages 3–4. I could not extract the PDF text myself (no PDF tool available), so someone should check it against the PDF before the hardware test.
- **Late RTU replies:** a reply that arrives more than 200 ms after a timeout is only rejected if its unit, function or length differ. RTU has no transaction ID, so this limit is recorded in the design.
- **Test dependency on Python:** the Rust-vs-Python validator comparison needs `python3` and prints SKIPPED without it.
- **Not built in this epic, as instructed:** the Tauri app, serial and Android transports, alarms, and the LAN and MQTT features.
- `research/02-standards-and-dashboard-design.md` has appeared in the repo (untracked, not created by me). `.kiro/steering/ui.md` still has a TODO to revise itself once it exists; I left that for the UI epic.
